headline_findings: Whoop 4.0 is built on the Nordic nRF52840 (64 MHz Cortex-M4F, 1 MB flash, 256 KB RAM) with a green+IR PPG, accelerometer and skin-temperature chip; Whoop 5.0 moved to an Ambiq Cortex-M4 MCU with integrated BLE, a TDK-InvenSense 6-axis IMU, and an Analog Devices PPG/ECG AFE plus 1 A buck-boost on a separate flex (verified: Nordic press release 2022-07; TechInsights WG50 teardown 2025).

Ring-class trackers prove the Nordic-class MCU + multi-path PPG can run 24/7 on tiny cells (Ultrahuman Ring AIR: nRF52840, 24 mAh, up to 5 days - verified Nordic 2023-09; Oura Ring 4: 26 mAh - secondary EDN/TechInsights 2024), while band-class devices land at 0.9-1.0 mA average draw (Polar Loop 170 mAh/8 days, Amazfit Helio Strap 232 mAh/10 days - secondary; averages are estimates derived from those figures).

Only two component prices were verified this session: nRF52840-QIAA-R US$6.78 at qty 1 and US$4.07 per unit on a 3,000-piece reel (Digi-Key, observed 2026-09-14) and Bosch BMI270 US$4.23 (Digi-Key product highlight, tier not shown); AFE, charger, battery and optics prices were NOT FOUND before the search budget ran out (verified anchors; everything else in the BOM is an estimate).

Minimum-viable band BOM (nRF52840 + BMI270 + integrated PPG module + NTC + 150 mAh Li-Po + charger + PCB + enclosure + strap + dock + packaging) is estimated at US$28-47 at 1k, US$20-33 at 10k and US$14-25 at 100k; a premium ECG/SpO2/skin-temp-IC/gyro band at US$38-68 / 28-47 / 20-35 (estimate; ex-works, excludes NRE, tooling, certification, duties, yield and logistics).

Peer-reviewed placement studies put the upper arm ahead of the forearm and wrist for PPG heart-rate accuracy under motion, with burpees and weight training the worst cases - so a lifting band should either sit on the upper arm (Whoop Body / Garmin Index style) or gate PPG during sets when worn on the wrist (verified: PMC12788198, JMIR Cardio 2025 PMC11951816, e-pan 2026 PMC13358589).

Whoop 5.0 samples PPG at about 26 Hz (secondary: the5krunner 2025-06-16); a 25 Hz continuous PPG plus 50-100 Hz accelerometer with gyro duty-cycled only inside detected sets is the industry baseline and fits a 150-200 mAh cell for 5-7 days at an estimated 0.8-1.3 mA average (estimate built from the verified capacity/life pairs above).

Zephyr/nRF Connect SDK already ships in-tree drivers for BMI270, BMI323, BMA4xx, ICM-42688, LSM6DSO, MAX30101/MAX30102 and TMP116/117/119, charger drivers for BQ2518x and nPM1100, the standard Heart Rate Service 0x180D sample, MCUboot + MCUmgr/SMP DFU over BLE, and Edge Impulse / TensorFlow Lite Micro (CMSIS-NN) targets for the nRF52840 - all verified on GitHub 2026-09-14; no in-tree driver exists for ADI ADPD4100, TI AFE4900, Maxim MAX86171/MAX86176 or PixArt PAH8013, so a premium AFE requires a vendor driver port (verified negative search).

Whoop's BLE protocol is a single 128-bit custom GATT service (61080001-8d6d-82b8-614a-1c8cb0f8dcc6) with command-to-strap, command-from-strap and data-from-strap characteristics and a 'sync batch data' message kind (secondary: gowhoop reverse-engineering repo, 2026) - the same pattern (standard HRS/BAS + one custom service with a rep-event notify characteristic and a batch-sync characteristic) is the recommended FitForge design.

The FCC grantee prefix given in the brief (2AI7N) does not match any Whoop filing; Whoop Inc files under 2AJ2X (2AJ2X-WS30 Strap 3.0, 2AJ2X-WS50 5.0 sensor device, 2AJ2X-WP40 4.0 battery pack), and the commonly quoted 638 mAh / 2.46 Wh figure is the slide-on Battery Pack 4.0, not the strap cell (verified: fccid.io; secondary: retailer listings).

Coverage caveat: the session-wide WebSearch budget (200/200) was exhausted after the first 15 queries and WebFetch is egress-blocked, so distributor price breaks for AFEs/chargers/batteries, analyst BOM teardown estimates, Whoop cell capacities, Oura/Amazfit MCU part numbers and India-specific component data are reported as NOT FOUND rather than estimated where no basis exists.

detailed_notes:
# Hardware architecture + BOM: screenless Whoop-class band (state of research 2026-09-14)

## 0. Coverage caveat
Fifteen web searches ran before the session-wide WebSearch budget (200/200) was exhausted; the two permitted WebFetch attempts (TechInsights, the5krunner) were egress-blocked. 'verified' and 'secondary' facts below come from search-result snippets of primary/trade sources and from GitHub code search (Zephyr, sdk-nrf, Edge Impulse, TFLite Micro, InfiniTime, gowhoop). Items not reachable are marked NOT FOUND. A few datasheet values recalled from memory are labelled RECALLED-UNVERIFIED and must be re-checked against the linked datasheet before use.

## 1. Teardown map (what is inside the benchmarks)
### Whoop 4.0 (2021-2024)
- MCU/BLE: Nordic nRF52840 (64 MHz Cortex-M4F, 1 MB flash, 256 KB RAM, 2.4 GHz multiprotocol radio) - Nordic press release 2022-07 (verified).
- Sensors: green + IR optical HR (PPG), accelerometer, skin-temperature chip; SpO2 via the IR/red path (Nordic PR, verified). PPG AFE, IMU and temperature-sensor part numbers: NOT FOUND.
- Battery: Sila silicon-anode chemistry, about 20 percent higher energy density (secondary); up to 5 days (verified). Strap cell mAh: NOT FOUND. The 638 mAh / 3.85 V / 2.46 Wh figure that circulates is the slide-on Battery Pack 4.0, not the strap (secondary, retailer listings).
- FCC: Whoop Inc grantee code is 2AJ2X (2AJ2X-WS30 = Strap 3.0, 2AJ2X-WS50 = 5.0 sensor device, 2AJ2X-WP40 = 4.0 battery pack); internal photos for WS30 and WS50 are on fccid.io. The 2AI7N prefix in the brief matched no Whoop filing (verified).

### Whoop 5.0 / MG (WG50 / WS50, 2025)
- Main board: Ambiq Micro ARM 32-bit Cortex-M4 MCU with integrated Bluetooth (Apollo4 Blue family; SKU not stated) + TDK-InvenSense six-axis MEMS gyro/accelerometer (TechInsights deep-dive teardown 2025; verified).
- PPG/ECG flex board: Analog Devices 1 A buck-boost converter + Analog Devices optical PPG/ECG analog front end (TechInsights; verified). Candidate parts are the ADI/Maxim MAX86176 or MAX86178 PPG+ECG AFEs (estimate, not confirmed).
- PPG sampling about 26 Hz; PPG PCB renumbered 820-000100 in the FCC filing (the5krunner 2025-06-16; secondary). Battery mAh: NOT FOUND.
- Architecture lesson: the 4.0-to-5.0 change swapped the nRF52840 for an Ambiq MCU (4 uA/MHz active, Ambiq product page, verified) and moved the analog front end to its own flex - that is how Whoop bought battery life plus ECG without a much bigger cell.

### Oura Ring 4 (2024) and Ring 5 (2026)
- 26 mAh cell, 18-path multi-wavelength PPG, a new smaller Bosch Sensortec accelerometer replacing Gen 3's BMI160, digital temperature sensing with an NTC thermistor (EDN / TechInsights / Creative Electron X-ray; secondary). MCU part: NOT FOUND in snippets.
- Ring 5 teardown: ARM MCU with 384 KB RAM, not repairable (Notebookcheck; secondary).

### Ultrahuman Ring AIR (2023) / Ring Pro (2026)
- nRF52840, 24 mAh Li-Po, up to 5 days, flex PCB with LED array + photodiode, inductive charging (Nordic PR 2023-09 verified; Becky Stern and Making Studio teardowns secondary).
- Ring Pro (May 2026): up to 15 days, dual-core processor, no subscription (the5krunner / Yanko; secondary).

### Amazfit Helio Strap (2025) and Helio Strap 2 (FCC 2026-05)
- 232 mAh, up to 10 days, BioTracker 6.0 PPG with 5 photodiodes + 2 LEDs, HR every second, HRV/SpO2/skin-temp/breathing at rest, BLE only (Wareable review, Amazon listing; secondary). SoC: NOT FOUND. Helio Strap 2 surfaced at the FCC 2026-05-28 as a BLE-only screenless sensor (Notebookcheck; secondary).

### Polar Loop (September 2025)
- 170 mAh, up to 8 days, 42 x 27 x 9 mm module, 29 g, WR30, Precision Prime optical HR + accelerometer, textile band with stainless-steel buckle, USB-C charging (SensorSpecs / GSMArena; secondary). Internals: NOT FOUND.

### Garmin Index Sleep Monitor (2025)
- Upper-arm band, up to 7 nights, internal antenna, FCC Part 15 Class B (Garmin product page and owner's manual; verified). Chips and cell: NOT FOUND.

### Open-source reference: PineTime / InfiniTime
- Firmware tree carries drivers for the HRS3300 PPG and BMA421 accelerometer (GitHub, verified) on an nRF52832 (RECALLED-UNVERIFIED). Useful as a hardware floor for a US$30-class device.

## 4. Power budget and battery sizing
Inputs: nRF52840 radio TX at 0 dBm 4.8 mA peak (module datasheets restating the Nordic PS; secondary); Apollo4 Blue Plus 4 uA/MHz active (Ambiq; verified). RECALLED-UNVERIFIED nRF52840 PS v1.11 values: CPU about 52 uA/MHz (about 3.3 mA at 64 MHz from flash), RX about 4.6 mA, System ON idle about 1.5 uA with RAM retention, System OFF about 0.4 uA; BMI270 about 685 uA with accel+gyro at full performance and tens of uA in accel-only low-power modes.
Field-derived averages (capacity / claimed life; estimate): Helio Strap 232 mAh / 240 h = 0.97 mA; Polar Loop 170 mAh / 192 h = 0.89 mA; Ultrahuman Ring AIR 24 mAh / 120 h = 0.20 mA (ring-class duty cycling). A 24/7 band with continuous PPG therefore lands near 0.9-1.0 mA average.
Budget for the FitForge band (estimate): MCU + BLE connection 0.15-0.40 mA; accelerometer at 50-100 Hz 0.02-0.10 mA (gyro adds 0.3-0.5 mA - enable only inside detected sets); PPG at 25 Hz continuous 0.4-1.0 mA (LED drive dominates; Whoop 5.0 runs about 26 Hz); PPG boost to 50-100 Hz plus rep-classifier inference during workouts adds 0.3-0.8 mA for 1-2 h/day; SpO2 spot checks during sleep (red + IR at higher LED drive) 5-10 mAh per night. Resulting average 0.8-1.3 mA.
Battery size: at 1.0 mA average, 5 days = 120 mAh and 7 days = 168 mAh; with 80 percent usable depth plus 20 percent aging margin, spec 150 mAh for 5 days or 180-200 mAh for 7 days. 100 mAh only reaches 5 days if the average drops to about 0.65 mA (Ambiq-class MCU and duty-cycled PPG). This matches the field: 170 mAh gives 8 days (Polar), 232 mAh gives 10 days (Amazfit).

## 5. Firmware stack (verified on GitHub 2026-09-14 unless noted)
- RTOS/SDK: Zephyr via Nordic nRF Connect SDK (Edge Impulse's official nRF52840 DK / nRF5340 DK firmware is built on NCS; repo active 2026-08). FreeRTOS stays an option on Ambiq (AmbiqSuite) but loses the Zephyr driver ecosystem (inference).
- In-tree Zephyr sensor drivers: BMI270 (Bosch 2021 / Nordic 2022), BMI323, BMA4xx (I2C only; SPI not supported), ICM-42688 (invensense,icm4268x), LSM6DSO, MAX30101/MAX30102 (touched 2025-2026), TMP116/117/119 (tmp11x + EEPROM). Charger subsystem: bq2518x, npm10xx (nPM1100), adp5360, bq24190, bq2429x, bq25713, pf1550, pca9422, axp2101, sy6974b, gpio.
- NOT in-tree (searched adpd, afe4404, afe4900, max86, pah8): ADI ADPD4100, TI AFE4900, Maxim MAX86171/MAX86176, PixArt PAH8013 - a premium AFE needs a vendor driver port (vendors ship reference drivers with eval kits; inference).
- BLE: standard Heart Rate Service 0x180D (BT_UUID_HRS_VAL) and Battery Service in samples/bluetooth/peripheral_hr (bt_hrs, bt_bas). Whoop's own protocol is a single 128-bit custom service 61080001-8d6d-82b8-614a-1c8cb0f8dcc6 with characteristics ...0002 (command to strap), ...0003 (command from strap), ...0005 (data from strap) and a 0x05 'sync batch data' kind (gowhoop reverse engineering 2026; secondary). Recommended FitForge GATT: HRS 0x180D for live HR, BAS 0x180F, plus one custom service with a rep-event notify characteristic (timestamp, exercise class id, rep count, confidence) and a batch-sync characteristic that streams daily aggregates in the fitforge.health.v1 shape - health data stays phone-local by design.
- OTA: MCUboot (sysbuild SB_CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_MCUBOOT) + MCUmgr/SMP point-to-point DFU over BLE; NCS 3.2.0 retuned MCUmgr BT OTA buffer sizes (CONFIG_NCS_SAMPLE_MCUMGR_BT_OTA_DFU_SPEEDUP). External QSPI NOR provides a full secondary image slot.
- On-device ML: TensorFlow Lite Micro with the cortex_m_generic target and CMSIS-NN optimized kernels (tensorflow/tflite-micro, active 2026-09); Edge Impulse wraps the same for nRF52840/nRF5340 and adds DSP blocks. Rep-detection model specifics belong to the rep-detection-science lens.

## 6. Enclosure, form factor, water rating, PPG placement
- Placement evidence: identical Whoop units on the upper arm outperformed forearm and wrist; burpees were the worst activity and the upper-arm Whoop still held up best (PMC12788198; verified). Proximal sites (upper arm, forearm) show fewer artefacts than the wrist; wrist motion and contact-pressure changes are the main artefact drivers (JMIR Cardio 2025, PMC11951816; verified). Accuracy dips during weight training and object picking (e-pan 2026, PMC13358589; verified).
- Implication for a lifting band: the IMU wants the wrist/forearm (bar-path and rep kinematics) but the PPG wants the upper arm. Options: (1) single upper-arm sleeve (Whoop Body / Garmin Index style) - best HR, bicep IMU still sees most compound and curl reps; (2) wrist band with PPG gated off during sets and HR back-filled from post-set recovery windows; (3) two pods (arm PPG + wrist IMU) - highest cost and pairing complexity.
- Materials: Polar Loop = textile band + stainless buckle, 29 g, WR30 (secondary); Amazfit Helio Strap = rounded rectangular module on a fabric band (FCC label drawing; secondary); Whoop = knit band with slide-on battery pack (secondary/recalled). Knit or textile breathes better under a sleeve; silicone is cheaper to mould and easier to keep IP68 at the buckle.
- Water rating: WR30 (Polar) is the only rating verified this session; Whoop IP68 / 10 m and other 5 ATM claims are RECALLED-UNVERIFIED. For a gym band, IP68 (1.5 m / 30 min) is sufficient and cheaper to certify than 5 ATM; swim use needs 5 ATM and a pressure-tested pogo seal.
- Charging: slide-on pack (Whoop), pogo dock with USB-C (Polar), inductive (Ultrahuman) - pogo dock is the lowest-cost sealed option; inductive adds a coil and roughly 1-2 dollars (estimate).

## 7. Recommended architecture for FitForge (synthesis, estimate)
nRF52840 (or nRF54L15 once priced) + BMI270 with gyro duty-cycled + integrated PPG module at 25 Hz (MAX86171-class with green/IR/red) + NTC skin temperature + 150-200 mAh cell + BQ25180 or nPM1100 + 8 MB QSPI NOR + LRA; Zephyr/NCS, MCUboot + SMP DFU, HRS/BAS plus a custom rep service, TFLite Micro classifier; textile upper-arm sleeve first (best PPG during lifting) with a wrist variant second; IP68. Likely BOM about US$25 at 10k and US$18 at 100k (estimate), before India-specific duties, BIS/WPC certification and tooling, which the india-manufacturing and india-policy-trade lenses cover.
